title: Generative AI floods and dilutes the market for books
byline: [Submitted on 22 Jul 2026 (v1), last revised 26 Jul 2026 (this version, v2)]
excerpt: Generative AI can produce book-length works of fiction at near-zero cost. These books are often dismissed as low-quality ``slop'' that buyers will ignore, and are assumed to carry little commercial weight. We test that assumption with full-text AI detection across 14,419 self-published genre-fiction books sold on Amazon from 2023 to 2026, matched to daily sales records through June 2026. None of these books disclose whether or not they contain AI-produced content. We find that books for which we detected substantial AI text ($>$ 25\%) make up a large share of the catalog but a smaller share of sales. Even so, they reach commercial scale, winning a growing share of sales over time and taking more of the scarce top-rank positions once held by books with no detected AI text. Over this period, the number of books with observed sales in a quarter grew 19.2-fold, while quarterly revenue grew only 8.9-fold. The market therefore added selling books faster than it added revenue, and revenue per selling book fell across most genres. Books with no AI text lose the most ground in genres with high AI diffusion, and most of all where Kindle Unlimited availability is high. Among top-selling books, those with substantial AI text draw on more distinctive language from existing books than do books with no AI text; for these books overlap rises with revenue, a gradient we do not detect for books with no AI text. Generative AI can thus reshape a creative market through scale rather than quality. Our results bear directly on the market-effect question at the center of the fair use defense to copyright infringement.

Abstract:Generative AI can produce book-length works of fiction at near-zero cost. These books are often dismissed as low-quality ``slop'' that buyers will ignore, and are assumed to carry little commercial weight. We test that assumption with full-text AI detection across 14,419 self-published genre-fiction books sold on Amazon from 2023 to 2026, matched to daily sales records through June 2026. None of these books disclose whether or not they contain AI-produced content. We find that books for which we detected substantial AI text ($>$ 25\%) make up a large share of the catalog but a smaller share of sales. Even so, they reach commercial scale, winning a growing share of sales over time and taking more of the scarce top-rank positions once held by books with no detected AI text. Over this period, the number of books with observed sales in a quarter grew 19.2-fold, while quarterly revenue grew only 8.9-fold. The market therefore added selling books faster than it added revenue, and revenue per selling book fell across most genres. Books with no AI text lose the most ground in genres with high AI diffusion, and most of all where Kindle Unlimited availability is high. Among top-selling books, those with substantial AI text draw on more distinctive language from existing books than do books with no AI text; for these books overlap rises with revenue, a gradient we do not detect for books with no AI text. Generative AI can thus reshape a creative market through scale rather than quality. Our results bear directly on the market-effect question at the center of the fair use defense to copyright infringement.

摘要：生成式人工智能可以以接近零的成本制作出长达一本书的小说作品。 这些书常常被认为是低质量的“废品”，买家会忽视，并且被认为没有什么商业价值。 我们通过全文 AI 检测来测试这一假设，对 2023 年至 2026 年在亚马逊上销售的 14,419 本自行出版的类型小说书籍进行了测试，与截至 2026 年 6 月的每日销售记录相匹配。 这些书都没有透露它们是否包含人工智能制作的内容。 我们发现，我们检测到大量 AI 文本 ($>$ 25\%) 的书籍在目录中占据很大份额，但销量份额较小。 即便如此，它们还是达到了商业规模，随着时间的推移赢得了越来越大的销售份额，并占据了更多曾经由没有检测到人工智能文本的书籍占据的稀有顶级位置。 在此期间，观察到的季度销售图书数量增长了 19.2 倍，而季度收入仅增长了 8.9 倍。 因此，市场销售书籍的增长速度快于收入的增长速度，大多数类型的每本书销售收入都出现了下降。 没有人工智能文本的书籍在人工智能传播度高的类型中失去了最大的优势，尤其是在 Kindle Unlimited 可用性较高的类型中。 在畅销书中，那些带有大量人工智能文本的书籍比没有人工智能文本的书籍从现有书籍中汲取了更独特的语言；这些书籍的重叠随着收入的增加而增加，对于没有人工智能文本的书籍，我们没有检测到这种梯度。 因此，生成式人工智能可以通过规模而非质量来重塑创意市场。 我们的结果直接关系到版权侵权合理使用辩护的核心市场效应问题。
